To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nuclear enhanced power corrections in QCD can explain the observed enhancement of longitudinal structure function  ( F L ) A / ( F L ) D, and suppression of transverse structure function ( F 1 ) A / (F 1 ) D.

the nuclear enhanced power correction to structure functions measured at large  Q 2 in deeply inelastic scattering in the leading logarithmic approximation in QCD is O ( α s ) and can be expressed as a sum of the nuclear enhanced parton distribution function  (PDF) and the Wilson coefficient function.
the nuclear enhanced power correction to F L, which is negative, and the correction to  F 1, which is positive, are both of the order of  O ( 1 / Q 2 A ).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure of hadrons and nuclei.
the study of nuclear enhanced power corrections in QCD.
a new type of nuclear enhanced corrections in DIS structure functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed HERMES data are consistent with QCD, and the nuclear enhanced power correction is the only mechanism which can explain the observed HERMES nuclear effect in σ A / A and R A / D.
the nuclear enhanced power correction to the longitudinal structure function F L is positive, while it is negative for the transverse structure functions F 1 and F 2.
the nuclear medium enhances power corrections in F L and suppresses power corrections in F 1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the nuclear enhanced power correction to DIS structure functions can be understood as the nuclear shadowing effect in the nuclear medium, and it should be taken into account when extracting parton distribution functions from nuclear structure functions.

the nuclear enhanced power correction effects are significant for the structure functions measured in the deeply inelastic scattering, and they can not be neglected in the global analysis of the parton distribution functions.
the nuclear enhanced power correction to the structure functions is the leading correction at order O ( α s Q − 4 / 3 ) to the leading twist approximation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the QCD power corrections in the nuclear medium are not negligible.
the power corrections are not small in DIS and should be included in the analysis of the structure functions.
nuclear enhanced power corrections can play a role in the analysis of nuclear structure functions and can lead to new insights into the nuclear structure of the nucleus and nuclear shadowing.
